name: form
title: Form
description: Forms on react-hook-form with a Standard Schema (Zod, Valibot, Effect): FormField binds one registry control by name, pending submit, server errors mapped to fields, a live root error, focus on the first invalid field, and messages in any language or i18n library.
docs: `<Form schema defaultValues onSubmit messages label>` with `<FormField name label description required>` around one control: Input, Textarea, NumberInput, Select, Combobox, Checkbox, Switch, RadioGroup, Slider, DatePicker, SegmentedControl, ToggleGroup or TokenInput bind by `name` (no `control` or `render`); `bind` or `render` for anything else, `useFormField()` inside a custom control. Give every field a default value. A field the schema rejects when empty (probed synchronously with the default values; Zod, Valibot and ArkType report every issue) gets a required marker, an `aria-hidden` asterisk in `text-destructive`, and its control `required`; `required` forces it, `required={false}` drops it. `requiredLabel` on the Form or field adds words for screen readers, like "required" in the page's language, which join the field's name; unset, screen readers announce the control's `required` state instead. `const { Form, FormField, useFormInstance, useFormWatch, useFormFieldArray } = createForm<typeof schema>()` types `name` against the schema's input; they are the same components. `onSubmit(values, { setError })` may return a Promise: the submit Button shows `loading`, fields are disabled (`disableWhilePending={false}` keeps them), a second submit is ignored. Throw a `FormServerError(message, fieldErrors)`, `{ fieldErrors, message }` or a Standard Schema issue list (`toFormErrors`) to put errors on fields and in `<FormRootError />` (an `Alert tone="destructive" live`); any other error shows its message there. Focus then goes to the first invalid field, or to the root error. Messages: `messages={formMessagesEs}`, a dictionary, or a function of the issue for i18next, FormatJS or Lingui (`createFormMessages(t)` makes one from `t(key, params)`, keys `form.<code>`); `FormField messages` wins over the form's. An issue is `{ code, field, label, params, message }`; codes: `required`, `minLength`, `maxLength`, `minItems`, `maxItems`, `min`, `max` (params `min`/`max`), `email`, `url`, `pattern`, `invalid`, `server`, or a schema message that looks like a key (`form.email.taken`), or a server error's own `code`. Schemas whose issues carry no code or params (Effect Schema) write the code into the message: `formIssueMessage("form.name.min", { min: 3 })` gives `@@form:form.name.min|{"min":3}` (a reserved prefix, never read from prose), read back as code `form.name.min` with `params.min` and no `message`; a built-in code works the same way (`formIssueMessage("minLength", { min: 3 })` gets the built-in translations). Unmatched, the key shows without its params. Inside a Form, `useFormInstance<Values>()` returns the typed react-hook-form instance (`trigger`, `setValue`, `getValues`, `control`, `formState`); its `watch` re-renders the Form, so read a live value with `useFormWatch(name)`. `useFormFieldArray(name, options)` is `useFieldArray` bound to the form: key rows by `field.id` (or, when the items carry their own `id`, by the property `keyName: "fieldKey"` names) and name their fields `items.${index}.title`. `form-context.ts` is internal; import only from `form`. Agents fill fields through their own parts and call the form's `submit` and `reset` when it has a `label`; `<FormActions tone="destructive" confirm="…">` puts `data-agent-confirm` on the submit button and hides the form's `submit` from agents. `FormActions disabled` (submit and cancel), `submitDisabled` (submit only) and `pending` (the pending look) reflect a busy state outside the form; while set, the form doesn't submit.
